newsitem.title: USA: Report paints mixed picture on Maine economy.
newsitem.headline: Report paints mixed picture on Maine economy.

text.p: Maine's economy turned in a mixed performance in 1996, with employment better than expected but with wage and income growth slower than hoped for, according to state economists.
The state's "very slow population growth" was the "greatest impediment to faster economic growth," according to the annual economic survey released this week by the Maine State Planning Office.
Maine's population increased by only 8,000 people between 1991 and 1996 compared with an increase of 64,000 people in the previous five-year period, according to the report.
The number of Maine residents between the ages of 16 and 24 years dropped by 11,000 between 1990 and 1995, "leaving a dearth of people in the labor force's entry-level age group," the report said.

Maine's had a 4.4 percent unemployment rate in 1996 compared with 5.7 percent in 1995. The lowest unemployment is in the southern part of the state while the highest unemployment was found in northern and Down East communities.
State economists said that because the unemployment situation saw its strongest improvement at the end of 1996, an improvement in migration paterns could give the state's economy "renewed vigor."
The wholesale trade sector of the economy saw the largest increase in payroll employment, 5.4 percent, while the manufacturing sector had the largest decrease - 2.8 percent, according to the report.
Personal income increased by 3.5 percent between the second quarter of 1995 and second quarter of 1996.
